primitives.name: Real-Time Multiplayer Room
primitives.verbatim_quote: # Game flow — `--type game` A game is a website whose template ships **realtime multiplayer rooms**.
primitives.assumptions: Rooms operate under shared global state with synchronized updates.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When concurrent actions exceed single-threaded processing capacity.

layer2.mapping: Each room is an isomorphic state machine with unique path-based identity.
layer2.telemetry: WebSocket connection count and latency per room

primitives.name: Rule Contract Enforcement
primitives.verbatim_quote: Two rules the checker cannot enforce and that decide whether the game is any good: - **`validateAction` is the only defence.** The client is untrusted and can send any action at any time.
primitives.assumptions: Client-side actions must be validated before state mutation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Upon invalid or malicious action submission.

layer2.mapping: The validateAction function defines the kernel of game validity by filtering inputs into admissible state changes.
layer2.telemetry: Number of rejected actions per session

primitives.name: Scaffolded Template System
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Create ```bash higgsfield website create --type game --category <genre> --subdomain <name> ``` - **`--category` is REQUIRED and must be a game genre** — `arcade`, `puzzle`, `shooter`, `platformer`, `rpg`, `strategy`, `racing`, `simulation`, `adventure`, `action`, `fighting`, `survival`, `horror`, `sports`, `card-board`, `education`, `endless-runner`, `moba`, `music-rhythm`, `sandbox-building`.
primitives.assumptions: All games inherit a standardized structure defined by category and template.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When non-compliant templates or categories are specified.

layer2.mapping: Each game category corresponds to a canonical template structure that governs its behavior.
layer2.telemetry: Compliance rate of category and template usage

The transition from legacy engines to unified website deployment implies a shift toward centralized control over decentralized execution. Rule enforcement relies on a dual-check mechanism: static validation via `bun run check:logic` and dynamic validation via `validateAction`. This ensures that while the system remains flexible, it maintains integrity through both compile-time and runtime checks. Failure modes arise when either validation layer fails, leading to inconsistent or exploitable game states.
